motif: the white pigeon (hook and last years); the AC motor in the middle chapters

beats.narration: [[room]]January 1943. Room 3327, a New York hotel. On the door, a [[dnd]]"Do Not Disturb" sign, three days old.
[[maid]]Inside, the maid found an 86-year-old man who had died alone. He couldn't pay his hotel bills, and [[pigeon]]his closest friends were the pigeons on his windowsill.
Yet today, [[grid]]the socket in your wall, [[motor]]the motors in every factory, [[car]]and one of the world's most famous car companies all trace back to his ideas, or his name.
[[name]]He was Nikola Tesla. So how did a man who shaped modern life die so poor? [[musk]]And why does the boss of the car company named after him say [[edison]]he's a bigger fan of Edison?
[[born]]Tesla was born in 1856 in Smiljan, in today's Croatia, the son of a Serbian priest. [[idea]]Young Tesla was already chasing a new kind of motor, turned by a rotating magnetic field.
[[ny]]In 1884 he landed in New York, and almost at once [[edison]]went to work for Edison.
[[dc]]Edison sold low-voltage direct current. Its weakness: [[copper]]sending power far took very thick copper wire, and distance got expensive.

[[myth]]Legend says Edison promised Tesla fifty thousand dollars, then joked, "You don't understand our American humor." [[book]]But in Tesla's own memoir, the promise came from a manager, [[notedison]]not Edison.
[[left]]Either way: no money. Tesla quit.
[[patent]]In 1888 he patented his AC motor, [[aiee]]and demonstrated it to America's electrical engineers. [[west]]One businessman saw its value: George Westinghouse.
[[cash]]He paid sixty thousand dollars in cash and stock, [[hp]]plus two fifty for every horsepower sold.
[[transformer]]With transformers, alternating current could travel long distances. [[shake]]Edison's business was under threat, [[war]]and the War of the Currents began.
[[elephant]]You may have heard Edison electrocuted an elephant to smear AC. [[fake]]That's a myth. [[y1903]]The elephant died in 1903, long after the war was over.
[[real]]But this is true: in 1888, [[brown]]engineer Harold Brown, using space and staff from Edison's lab, [[dogs]]publicly electrocuted stray dogs to make AC look deadly.
[[fair]]It didn't work. At the 1893 Chicago World's Fair, Tesla's AC system [[lamps]]lit tens of thousands of bulbs.
[[niagara]]At midnight, November 16th, 1896, power from Niagara Falls [[buffalo]]reached Buffalo. [[won]]AC had won.
[[tear]]And the story that he tore up his contract? [[waive]]In fact, when Westinghouse was short of cash, Tesla agreed to drop his per-horsepower royalty.
[[boat]]Then he dreamed bigger. In 1898, at Madison Square Garden, he steered a boat by radio, [[first]]one of the first wireless remote-controlled vehicles.
[[coil]]His Tesla coil threw crackling bolts of lightning. [[dream]]His real dream: send power and information around the world, with no wires.
[[morgan]]In 1901, J.P. Morgan put up a hundred and fifty thousand dollars, [[tower]]and Tesla built Wardenclyffe Tower. [[marconi]]That December, Marconi beat him across the Atlantic by radio.
[[stop]]Morgan stopped paying. The project stalled. [[blast]]On July 4th, 1917, the tower was dynamited, [[scrap]]and sold for scrap to cover his debts.
[[y1926]]In 1926, he predicted [[pocket]]a man would carry a wireless device in his vest pocket, to see and hear people far away. [[phone]]Sound familiar?
[[hotel]]In his last years he drifted between hotels, behind on rent, feeding pigeons. [[dove]]To nurse one injured white pigeon, he spent over two thousand dollars.
[[death]]On January 7th, 1943, he died in room 3327. [[court]]Five months later, the U.S. Supreme Court struck down part of a Marconi patent, partly because Tesla got there first.
[[relay]]But that doesn't mean Tesla invented radio. [[many]]Radio was a relay race of many inventors.
[[legacy]]So what did he leave us? [[socket]]Your wall outlet, for a start. Power grids still run mostly on AC.

[[motors]]Then, motors. The IEA estimates electric motors use over forty percent of the world's electricity, [[induction]]and the most common is the AC induction motor, Tesla's kind. [[ferraris]]To be fair, Italy's Galileo Ferraris invented it independently.
[[unit]]In 1960, the unit of magnetic field strength was named the tesla. [[mri]]A "3T MRI"? That's three tesla. [[patents]]In all, he earned 278 patents in 26 countries.
[[y2003]]In 2003, two engineers started an electric car company. [[acmotor]]Their cars ran on an AC induction motor, so they called it Tesla. [[y2004]]A year later, Elon Musk invested.
[[oatmeal]]In 2012, the cartoonist behind The Oatmeal crowdfunded to buy Tesla's last lab. [[backers]]Over thirty-three thousand people [[raised]]chipped in 1.37 million dollars.
[[donate]]In 2014, Musk gave a million dollars to the Tesla Science Center. [[page]]Google's Larry Page said he finished a Tesla biography at about twelve, [[cry]]and cried.

[[twist]]Here's the twist. Tesla's two most famous fans say the same thing. [[pagequote]]Page: "You don't want to be Tesla. You'd want to be more like Edison." [[muskquote]]Musk: "On balance, I'm a bigger fan of Edison than Tesla."
[[lesson]]They love his imagination, but learned from his ending. [[product]]Inventing isn't enough. You have to build it, sell it, [[survive]]and keep it alive.
[[note]]From Serbia's banknote, [[coin]]to Croatia's euro coins, [[airport]]to Belgrade's airport, [[gpu]]to NVIDIA's chips, [[everywhere]]his name is written all over today.
[[quote]]Tesla said: "The present is theirs; the future, for which I really worked, is mine." [[future]]We're living in it.
